title: Note two sides of a path
description: Write one difference between the two sides of a path.
oneStarDescription: Choose one spot on the path.
twoStarDescription: Write one difference you can see between the two sides.
threeStarDescription: Write one cause you will not claim from that difference.

title: Note who has the key
description: Write who has the key or the responsibility to leave the room as agreed.
oneStarDescription: Write the name of the person who holds the key or the booking.
twoStarDescription: Write whether the room should be locked, unlocked, or left as you found it.
threeStarDescription: At the end, confirm that state and write that you did.

title: Number steps on one drawing
description: Number three steps on one drawing in the order they are done.
oneStarDescription: Draw one view that can hold the steps.
twoStarDescription: Write 1, 2, and 3 on the drawing in the order of the work.
threeStarDescription: Ask someone to point to the steps in order, and fix a number that misled them.

title: Offer a smaller step
description: When a task stalls, offer one smaller step the other person can accept or refuse.
oneStarDescription: Say where the task stopped.
twoStarDescription: Offer one smaller step, not a new plan.
threeStarDescription: Do that step only if they want it, or stop.

title: Oil a dry spoon and wipe it
description: Rub food-safe oil on a dry wooden spoon and wipe off the excess.
oneStarDescription: Show the spoon is clean and dry.
twoStarDescription: Rub on a little oil and wipe until the surface is not wet.
threeStarDescription: Write the oil you used, from the container.

title: Open the file you sent
description: Open the file you sent and match one sentence to the draft you meant to send.
oneStarDescription: Open the copy that actually went, not the folder you think you used.
twoStarDescription: Find one sentence that matches the draft.
threeStarDescription: If something differs, write the difference before you send a correction.

title: Order objects by wear
description: Put three objects in order of wear and name the clue you used.
oneStarDescription: Choose three objects you may handle.
twoStarDescription: Put them in order from less worn to more worn.
threeStarDescription: Say the one clue you used, and one thing that clue does not prove.

title: Order six sketches
description: Order six quick sketches so another person can say what happened.
oneStarDescription: Draw six rough frames of one small event.
twoStarDescription: Put them in an order and number the backs.
threeStarDescription: Ask someone what happened, then say which frame they misread.

title: Overlap two color films
description: Overlap two pieces of colored transparent film and name the color you see.
oneStarDescription: Hold each film up and name its color.
twoStarDescription: Overlap them and name the color you see now.
threeStarDescription: Swap which film is in front and say whether the color changed.

title: Patch paper from behind
description: Patch a small paper hole from behind and write on the front.
oneStarDescription: Put paper behind the hole.
twoStarDescription: Write one word across the mend.
threeStarDescription: Say whether the mend is for practice or for a page you may alter.

title: Pick the explanation you can use
description: Read two short explanations and say which one you can follow without the author present.
oneStarDescription: Read two explanations of the same idea.
twoStarDescription: Follow one of them on a real example.
threeStarDescription: Say which one you could use alone, and the point where the other lost you.

title: Pick the latest name, then open it
description: Choose the latest of three files from the date in the name, then open it to check.
oneStarDescription: Read the three names without opening them.
twoStarDescription: Say which name looks latest.
threeStarDescription: Open it and say whether the content matches that date.

title: Pin a hem before you sew
description: Pin a hem on scrap cloth, check the length, then sew or unpin.
oneStarDescription: Pin the fold so it stays.
twoStarDescription: Measure or look at the length and move a pin if it is uneven.
threeStarDescription: Sew only if the pins are right, otherwise unpin and say why.

title: Place a song with a named clue
description: Name one musical or lyric clue and the period it suggests, marked as a guess.
oneStarDescription: Write the clue you can actually hear or read.
twoStarDescription: Write the period you would guess, with the word guess.
threeStarDescription: Write what you would look up before you treated the guess as a date.

title: Point with one arrow
description: Draw one arrow that touches the part you mean, and ask someone to name that part.
oneStarDescription: Circle nothing yet. Decide the one part.
twoStarDescription: Draw one arrow whose tip touches that part.
threeStarDescription: Ask someone which part you mean, and redraw the arrow if they miss.

title: Post the end time
description: Put the end time where a person who just arrived can read it.
oneStarDescription: Write the end time in the form the group uses.
twoStarDescription: Put it by the entrance or the agenda, not only in a message someone may miss.
threeStarDescription: Show a newcomer the time without a speech.

title: Press one leaf and date it
description: Press one fallen leaf flat and write the date you will look at it again.
oneStarDescription: Use a leaf that has already fallen.
twoStarDescription: Put it in a book or press with a note of the date.
threeStarDescription: On the date you wrote, say whether it stayed flat.

title: Put a known object for scale
description: Put a known object in the frame and say what size it gives the subject.
oneStarDescription: Choose an object whose size a viewer knows.
twoStarDescription: Photograph or draw it in the same plane as the subject.
threeStarDescription: Say one way the scale could still mislead.

title: Put the agenda at the entrance
description: Place the agenda where a person entering can see it without asking.
oneStarDescription: Write three agenda lines a newcomer can read.
twoStarDescription: Put it at the entrance you are actually using.
threeStarDescription: See whether one person finds it without help, or move it if they do not.

title: Read a closing date
description: Read a closing date on a notice and say what closes on that date.
oneStarDescription: Point to the closing date printed on the notice.
twoStarDescription: Say whether it is a form, a booking, a show, or something else the notice names.
threeStarDescription: Write the one action you would take before that date, or that the notice is not for you.

title: Read a contents page to a page
description: Use a contents page to find one section, then check you are on the page it named.
oneStarDescription: Pick one line in the contents.
twoStarDescription: Open the page number it gives.
threeStarDescription: Say whether the heading matches, or how far off you were.

title: Read a name on a bench
description: Read a dedication on a bench or similar gift and say what it does not tell you about the place.
oneStarDescription: Read the dedication that is there.
twoStarDescription: Say who or what the object is for, from the words.
threeStarDescription: Write one thing about the place the dedication does not explain.

title: Read a ratio as parts
description: Read a ratio such as one to four and say what one part means in the thing you are looking at.
oneStarDescription: Write the two numbers and what they refer to.
twoStarDescription: Say what one part is, using the label.
threeStarDescription: If the label does not say, write that you will not mix or measure from it.

title: Read a rule on a door
description: Read a rule posted on a door and say what you will do because of it.
oneStarDescription: Read the rule that is posted.
twoStarDescription: Say the action you will take or avoid.
threeStarDescription: If it conflicts with another sign, say you will ask rather than choose.

title: Read a year on a building
description: Read a year cut or fixed on a building and write one thing that year does not tell you.
oneStarDescription: Copy the year as it appears.
twoStarDescription: Write one thing the year does not tell you about the building.
threeStarDescription: Write one question you would need another source to answer.

title: Read feedback cards
description: Collect one sentence from each person on a card and read the cards without ranking the people.
oneStarDescription: Give each person a card and one question.
twoStarDescription: Read the cards aloud or to yourself without adding a score.
threeStarDescription: Group two cards that mention the same thing, and leave the names off if they were optional.

title: Read the decision back
description: Read the decision back in their words before you leave.
oneStarDescription: Write the decision using words they used.
twoStarDescription: Read it aloud before you end.
threeStarDescription: Change the sentence if they say it is wrong.

title: Read the time left
description: Read how much time is left until a moment you can see on a clock.
oneStarDescription: Name the time you are counting toward.
twoStarDescription: Read the clock and say how much time is left.
threeStarDescription: Look again near the end and say whether your first reading still fits.

title: Record their word for a symbol
description: Show a symbol and write the word the other person used, even if it is not yours.
oneStarDescription: Show it without saying your word.
twoStarDescription: Write the word they said.
threeStarDescription: Keep your symbol, add their word, or redraw, and say which you did.

title: Rehearse the cut on scrap
description: Make the cut on a scrap before you cut the piece you mean to keep.
oneStarDescription: Cut the scrap with the same guide.
twoStarDescription: Say what you would change.
threeStarDescription: Cut the real piece only if the scrap worked, otherwise stop.

title: Remove a mark that does not explain
description: Remove one decorative mark from a diagram and say what became clearer.
oneStarDescription: Point to a mark that does not explain a step.
twoStarDescription: Take it off a copy, not the only original.
threeStarDescription: Show the two versions and say what a viewer can see now.

title: Repeat a made-up fact
description: Repeat one invented fact in the same words when someone asks again later in the scene.
oneStarDescription: Say one invented fact once.
twoStarDescription: When asked, repeat that fact without adding a contradiction.
threeStarDescription: If you change it, stop and correct it in the scene.

title: Repeat the no
description: When someone declines, repeat the no and do not add a new offer in the same breath.
oneStarDescription: Point to the words they used to decline.
twoStarDescription: Repeat the no in a short sentence without a new proposal.
threeStarDescription: Wait for them to reopen the subject, or end the topic.

title: Repeat the word they used
description: Repeat the feeling or importance word they used, without adding your own.
oneStarDescription: Note the word they chose.
twoStarDescription: Use that word in your reply.
threeStarDescription: Ask whether that word still fits.

title: Rest a brush so the bristles stay straight
description: Put a damp brush where the bristles are not bent, and look at it the next day.
oneStarDescription: Lay or hang it so the bristles do not press on a point.
twoStarDescription: Say whether the bristles are still straight.
threeStarDescription: If they bent, show the new place you will use.

title: Retell from the other seat
description: Tell a small real event again from the place of another person who was there.
oneStarDescription: Tell the event in under a minute from your place.
twoStarDescription: Tell it again using only what that other person could have seen or heard.
threeStarDescription: Name one thing you left out because that person could not have known it.

title: Rinse a brush until the water runs clear
description: Rinse a paintbrush and stop when the water runs clear.
oneStarDescription: Rinse the brush in water until you can see the color leave.
twoStarDescription: Change the water and stop when a rinse stays clear.
threeStarDescription: Leave the bristles in their shape and say where you will put the brush.

title: Roll a ball on two floors
description: Roll the same ball on two surfaces and say which one slowed it sooner.
oneStarDescription: Use the same gentle push plan on both floors.
twoStarDescription: Mark where the ball stops on each surface.
threeStarDescription: Name the two surfaces in the note.

title: Roll two shapes
description: Roll two different shapes down the same slope and say which went farther.
oneStarDescription: Use the same start line for both.
twoStarDescription: Roll each once and mark where it stops.
threeStarDescription: Say one reason the winner might change if you rolled again.

title: Save a clip with its page
description: Save a short clip or quote only together with the page or person it came from.
oneStarDescription: Save or copy a short clip you might want later.
twoStarDescription: Put the page title and the date you saw it in the same note.
threeStarDescription: Ask someone to find the source from your note, or show that you can.
